title: Quantization profile operationalization: sweep harness, regression detection, and perf/quality matrix
creator: Liam Chen
description: Create an operational benchmarking harness and analysis pipeline to evaluate FP16 / INT8 / INT4 model variants under representative production loads. The goal is to produce a sensitivity matrix (quality vs throughput/latency) per model family and provide automated regression detection with CI and alerting hooks. This ticket covers: workload selection, sweep orchestration, metric collection (tokens/sec, p95 latency, tail latency histograms), quality metrics (accuracy/perplexity/ROUGE or task-specific metrics), data sketching for long-tail samples, and generation of artifact outputs (CSV heatmaps, dashboards, PR gating artifacts).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end harness can run a configurable sweep across FP16/INT8/INT4 variants for at least 3 representative workloads (chat, summarization, semantic-search) and export results to S3

Native metric collection includes tokens/sec throughput, p95 latency, p99 latency, success/error rates, and per-prompt quality scores; metrics are labelled by model, quant mode, batch size, and seq len
Automated regression detector that compares current sweep to baseline and raises an alert when quality drops by >2% absolute on key metrics or latency regressions exceed 15% p95
Artifacts generated: sensitivity CSV, heatmap PNG, and an HTML summary with top-10 failing prompts for any failing cell
CI integration: sweep runs on PRs touching kernel/quant code (smoke sweep) and blocks merge when regression thresholds are tripped
Dashboard prototype in Console showing matrix view and drill-down to per-prompt failures
Documentation (Confluence) describing methodology, workloads, and how to add new model families or prompt sets
steps: Define canonical workload corpus and prompt slices (short/high-latency, long-context, high-entropy prompts)
Implement harness runner that parallelizes across quant modes and batch configurations and records token-level timings
Integrate quality eval hooks (task-specific metrics) and canonical scoring scripts
Store raw traces and aggregated metrics to S3 / metrics store (prometheus + traces in Jaeger) and produce summary artifacts
Build regression detector service (stateless comparator + alert rules) and wire to Slack/ops-alerting
Add CI job (github actions) that runs a fast smoke sweep against a small sample on each PR touching runtime/quant modules
Iterate on visualization in Console: heatmap -> clickthrough to failing prompt examples
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff — collected candidate workloads: chat (2 datasets), summarization (CNN/News subset), search (MSMarco subset). Decided on initial metrics list.
2025-02-14: Prototype runner implemented (python) that spins 16 parallel jobs and records tokens/sec and per-request latency. Baseline FP16 run completed for small sample.
2025-02-16: First INT8 and INT4 conversions completed using quant-tooling v0.9. Observed ~2.4x throughput gain on INT4 for 512-token sequences but quality delta requires per-task scoring.
2025-02-17: PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3456) with harness and basic CSV artifact. Requesting review from runtime and eval teams.
2025-02-18: Review feedback from Eval (Sara Morales): add per-prompt scoring and ensure stable RNG for deterministic diffs. Action: add seed control and sample replay ids.

2025-02-19: Integrated p95/p99 histogram export to Prometheus and Jaeger traces for a subset run; created Grafana dashboard prototype. Noted noise on low-throughput slices — added warmup phase to runner.

2025-02-20: Implemented comparator that flags quality regressions >2% and latency regressions >15% p95. Still need to harden CI gating and flesh out Console visualization. Blocker: S3 lifecycle policy for storing large sweep artifacts (ops follow-up)
Next steps: finalize CI smoke sweep, add per-model baseline storage, and implement Console matrix view with clickthrough to prompt-level failures
